posts.caption:
There's a right month to change your booking system, and it isn't the busy one.

Nobody wants to be learning where the buttons are in the middle of their hardest week. So here's the honest test: think of your busiest stretch of the year, then count back three months. That's your window. If it lands on about now, this is worth a conversation. If it doesn't, tell me and I'll say so.

I'm not going to invent a deadline for you. There's no countdown here and no last-minute rush. The reason to move in a quiet stretch is just that it costs you nothing then, and it costs you a lot in the weeks you cannot afford to be distracted.

Setup is ten minutes on the phone. After that your hours, your team, your menu and your client list get moved across on my side, and you open it on the floor when you're ready.

$400 once, GST included. Then nothing, every month.

DM me the word DIARY and tell me when your busy stretch starts.

That's the whole calculation. Do it on your own number rather than mine — I don't know what you charge, and any figure I put in that box would be invented.

Work it out on your own ticket and you'll know more about whether this is worth doing than any pitch I could write.

posts.caption:
Four things that'll go wrong in your diary this week. None of them dramatic — that's exactly why they keep happening.

Someone gets booked over. Two names, one chair, one o'clock, and one of them finds out when she walks in.

Someone doesn't turn up, and nobody reminded her.

You move a booking to make room and forget to say, so she arrives at one for an appointment that's now at half past.

And a regular who used to come in every few weeks hasn't been for eight, and nobody noticed, because there's nowhere that would have told you.

Kairo answers all four. The diary cannot be double-booked. Reminders send themselves and every one gets logged. Move a booking and it stops to ask who to tell. And it builds the list of regulars who've quietly drifted, so you can send the message yourself.

$400 once, GST included. Then nothing, every month.

Tell me what this week actually looked like and I'll show you the same week in Kairo. DM me the word DIARY.
